correctness.rationale: For any fixed embedding of a non-induced simple H, conditioning on its e forced edges shifts each pattern vertex degree to d_v+Bin(n−1−d_v,p), leaving outside vertices unchanged. Summing (n)_h embeddings gives exact covariance (n)_h p^e b_k[Σ_v (k)_{d_v}/((n−1)_{d_v}p^{d_v})−h] for every n≥h, 0<p<1, 0≤k≤n−1. Removing zero-degree vertices gives F_k decreasing: −s if k<min positive d, unique crossing if min d≤k<n−1, positive if k=n−1. For induced P3, conditioning on two present edges and one absent chord yields (n)_3 p²(1−p)^(n−2)[2−3(n−1)p(1−p)], two roots (1±sqrt(1−8/[3(n−1)]))/2 when n≥4 (n=3 positive throughout); noninduced path one root 2/[3(n−1)]. Independent exhaustive exact rational enumerator checked 315 graph/motif/degree/probability cases n=3..5 and thresholds, distinguishing finite evidence from universal conditioning proof.
residual_risks: Exact finite verification cannot imply an unasserted parametrized generalization; all conclusions bounded as stated.

value.rationale: The question whether degree-class abundance aligns with arbitrary local motifs as edge density changes is natural in random-network dependence. A single exact formula yields a uniform all-n all-pattern one-switch sign theorem with sharp natural boundary: induced P3 already reenters at n=4. This contrasts two standard motif conventions and is a motivated qualitative structure result rather than the mere use of elementary conditioning.
residual_risks: Because the covariance follows short conditioning, an earlier exercise or mixed-moment identity in classical random graph texts may be equivalent; no universal historical novelty guarantee.
No transfer asserted to inhomogeneous edges, degree-conditioned graphs, or induced arbitrary motif monotonicity.
